pillar_reactions.evidence: The rep opened the pillar by tying it straight to the presenting problem — 'remember how you told me that like you have this lower back pains and waking up stiff' — and the prospect engaged by volunteering more symptoms mid-delivery, including the suspected sciatic pain down his left leg. He answered the 30-40 minutes, three to four times a week frame with 'Perfect', took the concept further himself ('the mobility and the strength, they are, you know, kind of married'), and responded to the 65-year-old-on-the-trail image with 'Yeah, that's what I'm going for, that's what I want.'

The weakest-fitting pillar for him and both parties knew it — he had already described eating roughly 90% clean, gluten-free, avocado and eggs daily, minimal processed food. He interrupted the delivery to add that he has been doing intermittent fasting for three or four months, and the rep folded it in ('you're going to just tweak that around'). Asked for questions he said 'No, that's pretty straightforward, man.' He had earlier said direction on nutrition 'would be, for sure, helpful', so it is accepted rather than objected, but it is incremental value on top of habits he already has.

He pre-sold this pillar himself twenty minutes before it was presented — 'I need a coach, man. That's what I'm missing' — and the rep opened it by naming that back to him. After the weekly check-ins, movement video feedback and direct cell number were described he said 'communication is huge in my life, in all aspects, so I'm glad to hear that he wants over-communication, because I think that's better than lack of communication.' Earlier, at the end of the nutrition section, he had already summarised the whole offer as 'it's all sounding exactly like what I really need when it comes to breaking it down to one thing. I'm just a person that can coach me and hold me accountable.'

anchors.raw: Once I signed up for the call and got all the information past the Facebook videos, all these other programs that I've looked into, they're all just like very cookie cutter. They're like, here's a program. Just follow it. And that's that. And that's why so many guys, you know, fall off of those
anchors.competitor: Generic online fitness and kettlebell programmes
anchors.note: He differentiated the offer in favour of the price himself, unprompted, before the price was named. Combined with his volunteered 'I need a coach', this was a prospect selling himself — which is why the price landed with no resistance at all.

anchors.raw: I see a PT every like two weeks, which is very helpful. He does a lot of drug dealing and we do some body work and some PT stuff. But what he just recognizes my low back is kind of... fuse is not the right word, but is like kind of connected to my pelvis where those should be kind of freely moving.
anchors.note: There is already a clinician engaged, biweekly, on the exact problem being sold against. Rather than treating that as a constraint or a party to coordinate with, the rep positioned the offer as the corrective to the PT's method: 'a lot of people are saying, oh, I'm stiff, I need to stretch a lot. No, you need to get stronger.' Commercially this defused an anchor; clinically it is the most exposed moment in the call.

anchors.raw: We just moved to a new house, and we have an actual, like, home gym, which I've been slowly putting together, it's pretty much, I just got the final piece, which is my pull-up bar... I bought some kettlebells, just haven't used them yet.
anchors.note: He already owns the equipment, the space and the kettlebells. What he is paying $6,000 for is programming and accountability alone, and he said so. The rep never had to defend that gap because the prospect had already concluded equipment was not his problem.

unmet_demand.want: Resolution of progressive low back pain that has spread up the spine, plus a new radicular symptom down the left leg he believes is sciatic
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme delivers strength work and coach-written mobility protocols. It does not assess or diagnose, it involves no clinician, and it does not coordinate with the physiotherapist already treating him. He was told 'the only way you don't get results in this program is if you choose not to show up', which is a claim about a spine nobody in the sale has examined.

unmet_demand.want: To pay the full $6,000 in cash forty-eight hours later, from house-sale proceeds
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The process requires payment on the call. There is no short deferral mechanism and no company instalment option, so the only route offered was consumer lending — which then failed twice.

unmet_demand.want: A programme that survives severe chronic sleep deprivation — he is woken nightly at two or three in the morning and cannot remember his last full night
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Sleep was never asked about and is not a pillar. It was volunteered as the single biggest driver of his fatigue, and fatigue is the reason he has not trained for two years, but nothing in the offer addresses it and nobody acknowledged it as a risk to adherence.
